label: original-phase bigram detector: n/k/f/p/o/x/u/d/q/1 shortly after t/k/w/v/i/o
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (98.7% of mass), never at t=0/1 or on the delimiter, and is close to silent during copy. Peaks at orig_idx 3-5. It acts like a conjunction over recent tokens: the current input is one of n,k,f,p,o,x,u,d,q,1 (n is strongest, 6x lift) and one or both of the previous two inputs is t,k,w,v,i,o (t is strongest, 7x lift as prev2_tok). The strongest activations come after runs of t (e.g. t t [n], t t w [f], i t t [k]). It mostly fires on the first occurrence of a token in the sequence. This predicate gets about 80% of the activation mass on dev but only 17% precision. Requiring BOTH previous tokens to be in the context set raises precision to 0.57 but cuts mass recall to 0.37. The unit looks like a graded, roughly additive response to recent-token identity, which boolean predicates capture only loosely.
